title: Tweezers
prompt: a pair of tweezers beside tiny beads on a table with three buttons: “Squeeze” closes the tips on a bead; “Lift” picks it up; “Release” lets the bead drop; see-through reveals the joined-end fulcrum and third-class lever action of both arms
blurb: A bead-gripping teaching adaptation of paired third-class levers shows how spring arms trade finger force for tip travel.
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / Levers

identity.note: Levers / Third-class levers, page 21, and Tweezers, page 23. Finger effort between joined-end fulcrum and tips gives lower tip force and greater travel.
identity.classificationNote: A named machine or diagram inside Levers is not a separate main chapter. The parking-meter heading is historical.

adaptationDecision.reason: Distinct paired third-class gripping application. Pliers place their hinge between effort and load. Nail-clippers add a separate operating lever.

prompt.note: Faithful labelled adaptation. The book grips hair; beads are a visible substitute that preserves lever geometry. Squeeze, Lift and Release preserve the grip cycle. Elastic arms reopen. Do not insert a pliers-style hinge between fingers and tips.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Bench or scale teaching adaptation of a named book example. Controls, fixtures and test specimens stage the lesson and are not claimed as the book apparatus.

truthNotes: The effective fulcrum is the joined rear. There is no central pin hinge or separate reopening spring.
A representative welded steel tool with integral tapered tips and grip ridges is drawn. The patent supports welded elastic arms, not the exact book construction.
Each finger effort point lies between the joined rear and its tip. The force arrows point inward. Both spring arms reopen when effort is removed.
Squeeze contacts the same bead on the table. Lift is user hand motion with the squeeze held. Release drops that bead and lowers the tool for another cycle.
The bead is a substitute for the hair in the book. The table, beads, slow motion, buttons and overlays stage the lesson. No hardware is invented for the anatomy count.
No precise force ratio is claimed for the flexible beam. Geometry and gravity are illustrative; motion is slowed for visibility.
Primary support covers 1998 and 2016 only. The 1988 edition remains inaccessible and unverified. No edition union is claimed.

supplementarySource.title: Dumont, Tweezers with interchangeable tips
supplementarySource.use: Only the description of elastic arms joined by welding supports the representative rear joint. The removable-tip mechanism is not used.
